intro: The Paediatric Early Warning Score is a bedside tool for spotting a deteriorating child on the ward before an arrest. It converts behaviour, cardiovascular and respiratory observations into a single number, with escalation attached to bands rather than to any single abnormal observation.
indications: Routine observation rounds on a paediatric ward
Deciding whether a child needs senior or critical-care review
Handover, where a trend in score carries more information than isolated vitals
Documenting an objective trigger for escalation
method: Behavioural, cardiovascular and respiratory components are each scored and summed. The app bands the total as low concern, caution, urgent review or emergency, and states the escalation implied by the band. A rising trend matters as much as any single total, so the score is designed to be repeated rather than taken once.
guidelineRefs: Monaghan A. Detecting and managing deterioration in children. Paediatr Nurs. 2005

faqs.q: What PEWS total should trigger escalation?
faqs.a: The app bands the total and names the response for each band. Local policy sets the exact trigger, so the banding should be read alongside your unit's escalation protocol.

faqs.q: Is a single high score enough to act on?
faqs.a: A high total warrants review, but so does a rising trend across observations. PEWS is intended to be tracked over time rather than used as a one-off number.
No. It is a safety net for structured observation. A clinician concerned about a child should escalate regardless of the score.

faqs.q: Are there different versions of PEWS?
faqs.a: Yes — several variants exist and units adopt local versions. The app states the components it scores so you can check it against your own chart.
